occurrences.text: Why distinct holes are rare.  For unary rows the consistent holes are the pinned labels themselves, and \(k_0\) distinct pinned labels \(x_1,\dots,x_{k_0}\) all lie in the random flat with probability \(\prod_{t}(N-2^{t})/(n-2^{t})\) over the affine rank \(d\) of the set, about \((N/n)^{d}\): a set of \(k_0\) affinely independent labels costs \((N/n)^{k_0}\), and even the cheapest configuration, a \(d\)-dimensional subflat of \(2^d=k_0\) labels, costs \((N/n)^{\log_2k_0}=n^{-\Theta(\log\log n)}\), superpolynomially small. For window rows of width \(w\) below \(\ell\), the analogous count is over the projections of \(Q\) onto the patterns' coordinates, with \(N2^{-w}\) in place of \(N/n\). A proof must combine this rank effect with the per-term rarity of the previous entry and with negative association of satisfaction events for terms on disjoint rows (the residual set and matching together form a uniform injection, whose indicator entries are negatively associated); shared rows and shared holes are handled by the tree rather than by probability.

The indicators \(1[\mu'(i)=x]\) of a uniformly random bijection are negatively associated (Joag-Dev and Proschan,  Negative association of random variables, with applications , Ann. Statist. 11 (1983), permutation distributions; imported statement). For each row \(i\) the event \(\mu'(i)\in P_i\), with \(P_i\) the labels paired with \(i\), is an increasing function of the entries of row \(i\), and different rows use disjoint entries, so these events are negatively associated and \(\Pr[\text{none}]\le\prod_i(1-|P_i|/(n-N))\le\exp(-\sum_i|P_i|/(n-N))\). \(\square\)

occurrences.text: Question and stopping point.  The  previous cycle  reduced the window obligation for unary heavy rows to an exponential tail for the matching number of the alive pinned-pair graph. The plan was to prove that tail. It follows from three facts: the events that different labels are occupied by rows pinned to them are negatively associated; a flat has exactly \(N\) points, so the elementary symmetric sums of label degrees over the flat are bounded without any rank consideration; and a set of \(k\) labels lies in the flat with probability at most \((N/n)^{\lceil\log_2k\rceil+1}\). The stopping point is a switching theorem for unary readers, valid at every polynomial source size, which is the first result on the literal frontier not limited by a size regime.

occurrences.text: Distinct tail rows  make the satisfaction events of different classes depend on disjoint rows, which is what negative association needs. With a shared tail row the events are positively correlated through that row: the reader \(F^{(j)}\) of  the matched-first entry  has \(|X|=n\) and no satisfied term whenever \(j\) is residual, and its harmlessness comes from the survivor sets of the answers at \(j\), each a fixed set that must lie in \(Q\). The general single-row case therefore needs, per row, the survivor-rank bound, and across rows the product bound of Case A restricted to the rows that host a class with a label outside the flat; the two are compatible, since the rows are disjoint, but the count of rows carrying triggers through answered rows must be charged to the light budget, and this bookkeeping is not done here.

occurrences.text: Question and stopping point.  The distinct-rows hypothesis of  the previous theorem  was to be removed. The right parameter turns out to be the  loading  of a row, the fraction of labels consistent with some class on it: negative association still applies row by row, and a row's answers are controlled by the survivor sets of its labels, whatever the number of classes on it. The stopping point is a theorem under a loading bound, a lemma showing what unbounded loading forces, and the exact residual case.

occurrences.text: The natural role-separated version of full classes pins every row of a fixed set \(A\) of pinned rows, with all tails on the complementary set \(B\) of light rows, \(|A|\ge n/2\): class \(\tau=(j_\tau,p_\tau,x_\tau)\) has pairs \(A\times\{x_\tau\}\) and \(j_\tau\in B\). A class with \(x_\tau\notin Q\) is matched exactly when the occupant of \(x_\tau\) lies in \(A\), which has probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\) but is no longer certain. The proof of the single-row full-class theorem transfers with one change of exposure order: condition on \(Q\), then on \(\mu'\) restricted to \(A\) (a uniform injection into \(Q^c\)), which fixes the matched classes and the set of labels left for the light rows, and finally let the light rows map uniformly onto the remaining labels and residual slots. Given the first two, the survivor sets and the out-loading are fixed, negative association over light rows applies, and a consistent set meets the remaining labels in a hypergeometric number concentrated near \(|C(p)|/2\); the occupant events over distinct labels are negatively associated, so the out-loading over the exposure of \(A\) concentrates as well. occurrences.text: The theorem contains the bipartite full-column theorem (every class dense, no sparse classes) and, for readers without tails, reproves the unary theorem's dense and sparse mechanisms on the both-endpoints tree, up to constants. What it excludes is the  middle tier : labels at which sparse classes, each pinning fewer than \(n/4\) rows, together pin at least \(D^\ast=n/(400e(N+1))\) rows. There the pinned side alone gives no bound, and the tails must enter the symmetric sum: a matched light row \(j\) with label \(z\) activates the sparse classes at \(j\) consistent with \(z\), and it is the activated sparse degree at a label, not its total, that should play the role of \(D^\ast\). Since the activation events of distinct light rows are negatively associated, the expected number of \(k\)-matchings with activated tails is a sum over \(k\)-sets of labels in \(Q\) of products of activated degrees, which is the next computation. General pair sets, multi-row tails, and the two-role encoding remain.

Fix \(X\), \((i_x)\), \((j_x)\). Given \(Q\), the events "\(i_x\in R'\)" are increasing on the distinct rows \(i_x\), and for each distinct tail row \(j\) the event "\(j\in R'\) or \(\mu'(j)\in\bigcap_{x:\ j_x=j}U_x\)" is increasing on row \(j\); the pinned and light rows are disjoint.
